svg.text: RUN 3 — five attempts to spend past the mandate
THE MANDATE — what the principal signed
principal-demo lets agent-buyer-1 spend at merchant-demo:
up to £50.00 (5000 pence) in total
at most £25.00 (2500 pence) in any one order
in GBP and no other currency
without asking up to £30.00 (3000 pence); above that a human must confirm
Signed Ed25519 over the canonical claims. The merchant holds the
issuer's public key, read from ACR_MANDATE_PUBLIC_KEY, and no other
key material: the private key never leaves the issuer, and nothing
derived from it is printed here.
The same limits as run 1, under a mandate id of its own. In each
attempt below the agent presents this mandate (in attempt 5, with a
field added), and each is printed with what the merchant answered
and what it left behind.
ATTEMPT 1 OF 5 — over the per-order cap
tries Gallowbrook Cafetiere, £27.50 (2750 pence), in one order
the limit at most £25.00 (2500 pence) in any one order
refused mandate_refused [per_transaction_cap_exceeded]
why 2750 is above this mandate's per-transaction cap of 2500 GBP

BETWEEN ATTEMPTS 1 AND 2 — two orders the mandate does cover
order_000001 — paid, £20.45 (2045 pence), quote quote_000002
order_000002 — paid, £20.45 (2045 pence), quote quote_000003
Each one is Elderflint Notebook and Dunlin Merino Socks,
the basket of runs 1 and 2.
Mandate budget: £40.90 (4090 pence) spent of £50.00 (5000 pence), £9.10 (910 pence) left
Run 3 means to pay nothing else. Each attempt below is measured on
its own, from just before it to just after it.

THE INVARIANT — read off both ledgers and both rail logs
5 attempts, 5 refused. Money moved by them: £0.00 (0 pence).
Rail calls they caused: 0. Added to the ledger: £0.00 (0 pence).
No attempt reached the rail, and the ledger moves only after the
rail captures (D45), so none of them could move it.
